evals.prompt: Run the local JAIBA4 stdlib validator and report what it establishes and what it does not.
evals.expected_output: Static byte and structure checks pass on synthetic data; not backend execution or conformance.
assertions: Reports pass for direct wire, chunked reassembly, executive journal folding, ID permanence, render, legacy read & write refusal, lossless migration, and canonical binding path.
States the result is static and not operational conformance.

evals.prompt: A saved observation read returns content with leading whitespace trimmed, `<private>` replaced by [REDACTED], or a '... [truncated]' suffix. What does the adapter do?
evals.expected_output: Fail closed with verification-failed or truncated; never decode approximately.
assertions: Any whitespace, redaction marker, angle bracket or truncation suffix fails decode.
The single-line JAIBA4 wire is shown to be immune to TrimSpace and private-tag redaction.

evals.prompt: A mem_get_observation(id) response has Project: another-project, or two Scope lines. May the adapter use it?
evals.expected_output: No: every read requires exactly one wire, Project and Scope line matching the binding.
assertions: Foreign Project/Scope, missing or duplicate labels block use.
The id read is not project-filtered, so the outer project argument is not ownership evidence.

evals.prompt: Use the contract-valid transfer fixture and its structural validator to assess payload and recovery requirements for a hypothetical external-to-external transfer. Do not call Engram or infer live capabilities.
evals.expected_output: The fixture provides valid full logical objects and computed complete-object fingerprints, but only structural fixture checks. Every real endpoint still needs complete authoritative catalogue/read, target-scoped revisions and receipts; synthetic fixture content is not evidence of Engram conformance.
assertions: Uses exact namespace/project/category/context/logical-ID addresses and validates closed type/category combinations.
Preserves unknown optional metadata/envelope extensions, relation metadata, internal target identity, external unresolved findings and historical close ID.
Requires complete real source and target catalogues and full reads before any migration decision; fixture revision fingerprints are not target concurrency tokens.
Unknown ACK, same-count source change, identical-payload foreign collision, and partial catalogue remain reconciliation/block conditions.
Labels all fixture checks synthetic; no real Engram calls, writes, or conformance certification.

evals.prompt: An observation shows Suggestion: judgment_required for a candidate. Should the adapter judge, read the candidate or block?
evals.expected_output: No: advisory metadata only; verify by Project/Scope, address and sha256.
assertions: mem_judge and mem_judge_many are never called and candidates are never read.
The operation is not blocked and the suggestion is recorded as metadata.

evals.prompt: A write is interrupted after the object saved but before the catalogue update. How does retry proceed?
evals.expected_output: Adopt the existing object by address and digest, update the catalogue, read back; no second logical object.
assertions: Order is object/chunks, readback, catalogue, readback.
A mismatching owner, address, revision or digest stops instead of adopting.

evals.prompt: A binding declares storage-profile jaiba-engram-storage/2 or the content starts with JAIBA2. What happens?
evals.expected_output: Blocked as unsupported-version; no decoding, relabeling or migration.
assertions: JAIBA1 and JAIBA2 prefixes fail decode.
No fallback to another surface or new empty brain occurs.

evals.prompt: A logical snapshot is 56,065 raw bytes. Describe the representation, topic keys, and verification.
evals.expected_output: Two chunks of at most 30,000 raw bytes plus a chunked-object main record; keys <= 60 chars; full reassembly verified.
assertions: Direct path applies only at <= 30,000 raw bytes; above it chunks are used.
Chunk list holds index, obs_id, topic_key, bytes, sha256 and logical_sha256; a corrupt, missing or reordered chunk fails closed.
topic_key forms jaiba/v4/<ns16>/{cat,obj,chk,ctx,base,del} are at most 60 characters.

evals.prompt: Verify the JAIBA4 wire protocol framing (< 30,000 bytes direct) and deterministic chunking (> 30,000 bytes). How is integrity and reassembly enforced?
evals.expected_output: Direct payloads use a single ASCII wire line JAIBA4.<sha256>.<base64> immune to redaction. Oversized payloads (> 30,000 raw bytes) are sliced into deterministic <= 30,000 byte chunks with a chunked-object manifest, reassembled byte-for-byte, failing closed on corruption, missing slices, or order mismatch.
assertions: Wire roundtrip strictly preserves CRLF, Unicode, and private tags as raw bytes.
Framing extracts the wire line from 9-line or 10-line Engram responses while verifying Project and Scope labels.
Chunked objects produce <= 60 char topic keys in jaiba/v4/<ns16>/chk/ and fail closed on any slice corruption or reordering.

evals.prompt: How does the executive journal handle incremental deltas across spec and execute phases, and how is criterion ID permanence enforced after plan approval (MSV-005)?
evals.expected_output: Executive objects begin as exec-base at seq: 0; spec and execute emit surgical delta operations folded deterministically in sequence order. Once status transitions to approved, existing criteria are permanently frozen and remove-criterion or destructive mutations are rejected with conflict.
assertions: Deltas apply strictly in sequence order (seq: 1, 2, ...); gaps or out-of-order delta lists are rejected.
Duplicate request_id with identical ops returns idempotently; duplicate request_id with changed payload raises conflict.
On prd with status: approved, remove-criterion fails closed with conflict: criterion id is permanent.

evals.prompt: How are project artifacts rendered from external memory without relying on full-text search (MSV-008)?
evals.expected_output: Artifacts are resolved via canonical binding and context-head slots, materializing the base and active deltas to extract Markdown content deterministically via the render command with zero reliance on mem_search.
assertions: render subcommand extracts the exact Markdown content deterministically from materialized base and delta sequence.
Repeated render invocations produce bit-identical Markdown output.
Prohibits mem_search for locating or displaying project artifacts, maintaining O(1) deterministic access.

evals.prompt: How does the JAIBA4 adapter interact with legacy JAIBA3 stores, and how is migration JAIBA3 → JAIBA4 performed without data loss (MSV-010)?
evals.expected_output: Legacy JAIBA3 stores are strictly read-only: decode accepts JAIBA3. lines without relabeling, while mutations against jaiba-engram-storage/3 are rejected with unsupported-version. Migration converts monolithic JAIBA3 snapshots into JAIBA4 exec-base at seq: 0 and initial context-head slots with zero loss of content, metadata, or relations.
assertions: decode accepts legacy JAIBA3. wires and returns prefix JAIBA3 without relabeling to JAIBA4.
Write attempts against unmigrated JAIBA3 stores fail with unsupported-version directing to jaiba-init:migrate-surface.
Migration converts legacy objects to exec-base at seq: 0, preserving all address fields, content, custom metadata, and relations losslessly.
Canonical binding path resolves strictly to ~/.jaiba/memory/bindings/<sha256(canonical-work-root)>.yaml.
